title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: 8 July 1986. This is Digression 3 of Grothendieck's notes on 'magiciens' and 'ateliers'. These are his combinatorial axiomatics for 'multistructures'. There is a set M of structures with a domination relation ≪, a closure operation Δ, a relation ≤°, a realisation |·|, and for each X a set X̃ of sub-structures. A 'magicien' adds a family 𝓕 of admissible figures, and an 'atelier' is roughly such a family closed under the relevant operations. The previous page adds a 'compactologie': a subset M_c ⊂ M of 'compact' structures. Axiom Mag cpct 1 has three parts: (a) X ∈ M_c implies X̃ is finite; (b) M_c is closed downward under ≪. A compatibility axiom ('Mag et cpct') relates M_c and 𝓕.

This page:
(1) Definition. Fix M_c. A part 𝓛 ⊂ M is locally finite if, for every compact X, the set 𝓛_X = {Y ∈ 𝓛 | Y meets X} is finite. Here Y ‖̄ X means 'not disjoint', i.e. the realisations meet. This is the exact analogue of a locally finite family of subsets: every compact set meets only finitely many members.
(2) The locally finite parts form an 'antifiltre', i.e. an ideal of the power set (closed under subsets and finite unions).
(3) The set 𝓕_lf(M) of locally finite figures forms an M-atelier, provided M ⊂ 𝓕_lf(M). This proviso is stated as a new axiom, Mag cpct 1 c): for each X ∈ M, X̃ is locally finite, i.e. for every compact Y only finitely many X' ∈ X̃ meet Y.
(4) If 𝓛 is a locally finite pre-figure, its Δ-closure is again locally finite.
(5) The compatibility axiom says exactly 𝓕 ⊂ 𝓕_lf. Hence 𝓕_lf is the largest atelier (over M) compatible with the given compactology.
(6) Conversely, start from (M, Δ, ≤°, |·|, 𝓕). The largest compatible compactology is M_c = {X | for all F ∈ 𝓕, {Y ∈ F | X meets Y} is finite}.

Together, (5) and (6) form the two sides of a Galois correspondence. It is induced by the relation 'X meets only finitely many members of F', between compactologies and ateliers. This is the combinatorial shadow of the duality between compact sets and locally finite families, as for locally finite CW complexes.

The next page checks the axioms for this M_c. It notes that M_c cannot reasonably be defined from the structural data alone without 𝓕. Its example is an ordered set without both endpoints, where only points and segments I_{a,b} should be compact.
errors: Step (4), stability of local finiteness under Δ-closure, needs axiom 1 c). A compact Y meeting X' ≪ Z, with Z ∈ 𝓛, meets Z, so only finitely many such Z occur. But Z̃ may be infinite, so one also needs Z̃ locally finite to conclude. The page uses this implicitly.
The claim that the M_c of (6) satisfies Mag cpct 1 a) requires taking F = X̃ ∈ 𝓕 (as the next page says). So it relies on M ⊂ 𝓕 being part of the magicien axioms; otherwise a) can fail.
The phrasing 'à condition ... de supposer ... que M ⊂ 𝓕_lf(M)' is garbled. The intended statement is that 𝓕_lf(M) is an M-atelier under the extra axiom 1 c).

ideas.what: Locally finite family relative to a chosen class of 'compact' structures (each compact meets finitely many members)
ideas.modern_name: locally finite family / locally finite cell complex; compactology or bornology
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical point-set topology (locally finite covers: Dieudonné, Stone); 'compactologie' used by Buchwalter and Waelbroeck c. 1969-71 in functional analysis

ideas.what: Locally finite parts form an ideal ('antifiltre')
Galois correspondence between compactologies and ateliers: the largest atelier compatible with a compactology, and the largest compactology compatible with an atelier
ideas.modern_name: polarity / Galois connection induced by a binary relation (as in formal concept analysis); compact-vs-locally-finite duality
ideas.usually_credited_to: general polarity construction (Birkhoff); the specific instance is folklore in topology

ideas.what: Axiomatic combinatorial framework of 'magiciens/ateliers' with an added compactness structure, intended to model locally finite complexes and subdivisions combinatorially
ideas.modern_name: combinatorial models for tame topology / abstract cell complexes; related to the 'topologie modérée' programme of the Esquisse
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (unpublished, 1986); loosely comparable to abstract cell complexes (Tucker, Kovalevsky) and o-minimal tame topology (van den Dries)
ideas.where_published: The Esquisse d'un programme (1984) calls for a 'tame topology' but, as far as I know, does not contain this formalism

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 1986 'magicien compactologiste' theory equips combinatorial multistructures with a compactology. It pairs this with locally finite figures via a Galois correspondence. A Borel-Lebesgue-type axiom (Mag cpct 2) and a 'richness of M_c via subdivisions' axiom are announced on the previous page but not given here. The programme seems to be a combinatorial foundation for locally finite (non-compact) tame spaces; it is unpublished and has not been developed.
missed.quote: Ainsi 𝓕_loc fin est le plus grand atelier dominant M, qui soit compatible à la compactologie.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a piece of the little-known 'ateliers' project towards a combinatorial tame topology. Historians and those studying Grothendieck's post-Esquisse foundational ideas may find the explicit compact/locally-finite duality useful, though the mathematics on this page is itself elementary.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is elementary: locally finite families, an ideal, and a standard polarity. Its interest is mainly as documentation of the unpublished 1986 'ateliers/magiciens' framework and Grothendieck's choice of the term 'compactologie', not as a new result.
transcription_corrections: 'Mégacrit 4 c)' should read 'Mag cpct 1 c)'. It is the third part of axiom Mag cpct 1 from the previous page.
'L'axiome Mégacrit signifie' should read 'L'axiome Mag et cpct signifie' (or 'Mag cpct'), referring to the compatibility axiom of the previous page.
'des fragments loc. finis' is likely 'des figures loc. finies'. Likewise 'préfragment' is likely 'préfigure'.
The '𝓛' symbols are a script/underlined 𝓛 (or 𝓢) as written; '𝓕_{ℓf}(M)' appears as 'F_{lf}(M)'.
On the next page, 'convictologies/convictologie' should read 'compactologies/compactologie'.
The garbled '{+M-+}atelier[?], à condition[?] pourvu[?] de supposer[?] ... l'exige[?] ensuite[?]' reads roughly 'forme un M-atelier, à condition de supposer (ce qui exige ...) que M ⊂ 𝓕_lf(M)'.
